pages.text: "I will not go! More snow for my tower!" Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, stacked snowballs outside the shop. The alley grew dark.
Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, jingled the bell. "Time to go, Nono." "Mine will be the tallest today!" Nono shook his head and hugged the tower.
His eyes half closed. His body leaned sideways. His shaky hands dropped a snowball, and the tower collapsed. "I am not sleepy... Why are my hands doing that?"
Grandpa Badger took the awning rope. "Children, the awning is coming down." Slowly, it lowered.
One alley lamp lit, then another. Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, put on the bag. "Awning down means time for sleep."
Gugu held Nono's hand. "Let us go too." Nono set one snowball on the tower and let go. Yawn! His beak opened wide all by itself.
Grandpa lit the alley with a lantern. The three walked side by side beneath the lights. Snow crunched underfoot.
At his home under the roof edge, Nono slipped beneath his dry-grass blanket. The alley lamps shone up to his home. "Sleep well too, snow tower," he whispered.
Next evening, the awning lowered again. Nono set down a snowball and stood first. "One, stop playing! Two, follow the lamps home! Three, under the blanket!" Gugu and Kiki followed.
In the morning sunshine, Nono built the tallest tower. Gugu and Kiki ran up and hugged him. Early sleep gives you morning energy. He touched his green scarf. "Awning down, time for sleep!"
